title: Horse Barn Burial Site
summary: In 2003, a group burial was discovered during residential development and barn construction on Shelter Island, dating between about 1400 and 1640. Shinnecock tribal members argued against further disturbance and treated the area as a cemetery. Despite their resistance, development continued, and the remains were reburied in an undisclosed location on Shelter Island.

why_this_matters: The tragic disruption of a sacred 1400 AD group burial to construct a residential horse barn in 2003 occurred despite fierce protests from Shinnecock tribal members. Acknowledging this desecration highlights the ongoing vulnerability of Indigenous resting places on private property and the urgent need for stronger legal protections for Native American cemeteries.
